- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model fails to capture sharp downward momentum, often lagging by 1–3 days.
- Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- Reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment turns negative within 3 days — model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts.
- Avoid extrapolating upward from recent highs — if last 3 prices are rising, cap forecast at +5% above recent peak unless sentiment remains strong.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 10–15% to account for structural bearish bias.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is 2–3 days below forecast, adjust next forecast down by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
